trans-unit.source: Faceted full-text search backed by Meilisearch.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: search the site index and ask an LLM to summarize the matching documents.
Iterates all sites (or a single site) and re-pushes every indexed record to Meilisearch.
Empty = all sites. Otherwise the TYPO3 site identifier (matches the directory under config/sites/).
Drop and recreate the Meilisearch index before populating. Use only after schema changes — the index is unavailable for the duration.
Leave the configured embedder settings untouched on Meilisearch. Use when troubleshooting a wedged hybrid setup.
Index status and ad-hoc search / RAG testing.
Site "%s" is not configured for Meilisearch.

Promotes or demotes this record in search results. Composes multiplicatively with the per-type default configured in Site Settings. Has no effect unless the integrator has enabled the boost ranking rule.

Document ids that must appear in the retrieved context for this question. Comma = all required, pipe = any one is enough (e.g. "help-761, help-780|help-132"). The pipe form matters because the same topic exists once per product and per medium. Checked by ws_meilisearch:retrieval-check without an LLM call. Leave empty to skip the retrieval check for this test.

How much of the retrieved context must come from the right subject area, as "<min>:<pattern>", comma-separated for several rules (e.g. "4:daVo" or "3:schema"). The pattern is matched case-insensitively against a document\'s id, title and helpSourcePath, so a DITA chapter code works as well as a word. Catches a context where the one expected document ranks first but the remaining slots are filled with unrelated topics. Leave empty to skip.
Synonym = the term expands to the words on the right. Single token = never split this character sequence (product keys, parameter names). Stop word = ignore the word while indexing and searching.
What visitors type. Lowercase; matching is case-insensitive.
One word or phrase per line. A search for the term above also matches documents containing these. Add the reverse direction as its own record if it should work both ways.
Only "active" records are pushed to the search engine. "Candidate" is a machine proposal waiting for review, "rejected" keeps it from being proposed again.
Leave empty to apply to every site of this installation.
Hand-written knowledge the chat assistant answers from
What the entry is about, phrased the way a customer would ask, e.g. "Which operating systems are supported?"
The information itself, in complete sentences. The assistant reads exactly this text — write it as you would explain it to a customer. One topic per entry.
Synonyms and wordings customers use, comma-separated, so the entry is found even when the question uses different words.
Why the entry exists, who confirmed it. Never shown to the assistant.
Chat conversation this entry was written for (see the chat protocol).
Keep it high so hand-written knowledge wins over imported documentation on the same topic.
No protocol found for this id.
Only administrators may manage MCP accesses.
The title must not be empty.
The selected backend user does not exist or is disabled.
Write access requires a backend user.
The expiry date must have the format YYYY-MM-DD.
You are not allowed to view knowledge entries.
You are not allowed to create knowledge entries.
No site you have access to was found.

Entry not found or no permission.

Submitted via the MCP interface, not by a visitor
One row is stored per chat turn. The protocol contains the full wording of the visitors (personal data).
Not enabled on any site. Site setting:

Via the MCP interface, AI clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, the Claude API) can query the chat assistant, search the index, read the chat protocol and maintain the chatbot knowledge — depending on the access rights. Create a separate access token for each client or person so that it can be blocked individually. The token is only displayed once. Write operations run as the selected backend user and appear under that user’s name in the history.
New access token “%s” — copy the token now, it will not be shown again:
The token will no longer work afterwards. This cannot be undone.
No MCP access tokens have been created yet.
Recommended: create a dedicated non-admin user who only has permissions on the tx_wsmeilisearch_knowledge_entry table.

Entries are used by the chat assistant as knowledge sources (not shown as search hits or sources) and indexed when saved. Please write full sentences in the language of the entry; one topic per entry; in the “Alternative wordings” field, add synonyms and phrasings that customers use.
You do not have access to a site.
“%s” will be deleted and removed from the search index.
A maximum of 500 entries is shown.
Site "%s" is not configured for Meilisearch.
Meilisearch client could not be created (check meilisearch.url / key).
Site "%s" has no RAG provider configured.
RAG ping for "%s" succeeded in %d ms — reply: "%s"
RAG ping for "%s" failed after %d ms: %s
%s: imported %d, skipped %d, media attached %d. Run reindex to push them to Meilisearch.
Purge skipped — confirmation checkbox was not ticked.
Purged %d knowledge resource row(s) for language %d. Re-run reindex so Meilisearch drops the orphaned doc IDs too.
Test #%d has no last_actual_answer yet — run the test first, then adopt.
Test #%d already matches the last actual answer — nothing to adopt.
"%s" — adopted last actual answer as new expected (%d→%d chars). Re-run to confirm.
Plain typo-tolerant full-text search across pages, news, and indexed files.
Same query restricted to `type=file` — handy for "find me the PDF".
Empty query + sort descending. Surfaces the biggest indexed binaries.
Empty query → all docs, walk pages with Prev / Next at the bottom.
Vector + keyword blend — finds docs even when the wording is paraphrased.
Needs an embedder configured. The toggle stays a no-op on sites without one.
LLM-grounded answer with cited sources, retrieval bias toward the question topic.
Needs a RAG provider configured. Click anyway to see the "disabled" status.
Page id where the records live. 0 = site root.
When off, every knowledge resource starts with an empty title.
A folder containing an index.html TOC and a <langDir>/topics/*.html tree (the standard DITA-OT XHTML output).
Absolute or relative to project root. Must contain index.html and the language subdir.
Subdirectory under --path that contains topics/ and figures/.
Recommended — wipes existing rows for the chosen language so re-runs are idempotent.
Only import the first N topics. 0 = no limit.
Where the topic-specific media subfolders are created in fileadmin. Empty = site default (meilisearch.knowledgeResource.fileadminFolder).
Walk a fileadmin folder and create one knowledge resource per file. Reuses existing FAL records.
FAL folder containing the files to import. Existing sys_file records are reused; nothing is copied.
Walk into subfolders recursively. Off by default — keeps re-runs predictable.
When off, every knowledge resource starts with an empty title — only useful if you plan to edit them manually afterwards.
One curated document at a time — PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, Office, EPUB, plain text.
Empty = file name. Drives how the entry appears in search results.
Optional one-paragraph summary shown as the snippet in results.
Where the uploaded file lands in fileadmin. Empty = site default (meilisearch.knowledgeResource.fileadminFolder). The "uploads/" subfolder is added automatically.
Fetch a list of URLs and create one knowledge resource per response — body via Tika, source kept in FAL.
One URL per line. Only http/https. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped.
Where downloaded files land in fileadmin. Empty = site default (meilisearch.knowledgeResource.fileadminFolder). A "urls/" subfolder is added automatically.
Per-URL fetch timeout. Slow servers fail individually without wedging the whole batch.
Responses larger than this are aborted and counted as skipped.
Upload one .zip containing many documents — each entry becomes its own knowledge resource.
A .zip archive containing the documents to import.
Where the extracted files land in fileadmin. Empty = site default (meilisearch.knowledgeResource.fileadminFolder). A "zips/" subfolder is added automatically.
Off (default) flattens the zip — every file lands directly in zips/. On mirrors the zip's directory structure.
No data in the selected time period.
No zero-result queries — everything is found.
No RAG requests in the selected time period.
Submits to the same Test view; the answer renders below the search results.
Retrieval returned no documents for this question — the LLM was not called.
Click any preset to run it. Tags show which phase / feature it demonstrates.
Replace the expected answer with the latest actual. Use only after manually verifying the actual is factually correct.
Run this test now (calls the RAG provider once).
Replace the expected answer with the last actual answer for this test? Make sure the actual answer is factually correct — it becomes the new regression baseline.

Embedder + RAG state per site, live from the Meilisearch server. Use the maintenance buttons to force-push the embedder configuration (in case it drifted out of sync) or probe the LLM provider with a minimal "ping" round-trip.
Not applied yet. Click "Re-push" to write it.
No embedder configured for this site — keyword search only.
No RAG provider configured for this site.
Individual records (boost field, hidden flag, manual overrides) are managed in the standard List module:
Open knowledge resources in the List module
One index per site, faceted by record type. The columns below reflect the live state of each Meilisearch index plus the configured embedder / RAG provider from the site settings.
Drop and recreate the %s index? Search is unavailable during the rebuild.
Live status of each site index directly from the engine (uncached): documents, indexing status, distribution by type, task queue including latest errors, and a settings snapshot.
Short name of the test, shown in the test list.
Asked exactly like a visitor in the chat would ask it.
Reference answer. The actual answer is compared with it by meaning (embedding similarity), not word for word.
Minimum similarity (0–1) for the test to pass. 0.85 suits most questions; lower it for questions that can be answered in many wordings.
Identifier of the site whose index and assistant the test runs against.
Runs all enabled RAG tests of a site and stores score and actual answer, so changes of model, prompt or index show up as regressions.
Reindex is NOT triggered automatically — run ws_meilisearch:reindex (or use the Overview tab) afterwards to push the imported documents to Meilisearch.
No Meilisearch is configured for this site (meilisearch.url is empty).

Aggregated FE search queries from tx_wsmeilisearch_search_log. Opt-in per site via meilisearch.analytics.enabled = true. Only {query, result count, site, language, source, timestamp} are stored — no IPs, no user IDs.
Analytics is currently not enabled on any site. Set meilisearch.analytics.enabled: true in the site settings so that future search requests are logged.
For each answered RAG request one row with source='rag' is stored ({question, status, number of context hits, number of cited sources, hybrid, time}) — no answer text.

Help topics live in tx_wsmeilisearch_knowledge_resource and are pushed to Meilisearch as a separate document type (type=help). Individual records can be adjusted in the List module — boost, hidden flag or abstract overrides survive the next import only if the identifier stays unchanged.
One card per registered KnowledgeResourceSourceImporter. New importers added in PHP appear here automatically — no template change needed.
Hard-deletes every knowledge resource row in the chosen language together with its FAL references. Meilisearch keeps the now orphaned help-<uid> document IDs until the next reindex.
I understand that this deletes all knowledge resource rows of the selected language.

Quality-assurance harness for the RAG pipeline. Each row in tx_wsmeilisearch_ragtest is a triple of question, expected answer and threshold; “Run” asks the RAG provider the question and scores the actual answer against the expected one via embedding cosine similarity. A score below the threshold means the model, prompt or corpus has drifted away from the expected answer — a real quality regression. The scheduler task runs the same engine on a schedule; this tab is for ad-hoc triage.
No regression tests defined yet. Click + New test to add the first one (you need a question, the expected answer and a similarity threshold — 0.85 is a sensible default).
Set meilisearch.rag.provider in this site's settings.yaml to enable RAG.
